archetype.name: Improviser (holds it, scrambles out)
archetype.definition: Watson waits for something downfield and breaks the pocket when it isn't there. That buys him scrambles and some explosive throws, and it also gets him sacked more than almost any qualifier.

report.headline: When the pocket holds he's efficient; when it doesn't, the sacks swallow everything.
report.take:
Watson's 2026 depends almost entirely on how often he is pressured. In the two games he was barely touched, he played like his Houston self: an 11.4% pressure rate against Tampa Bay brought +10.4 passing EPA, and 10.8% against Pittsburgh brought +9.2. In the games where the rush got home, he fell apart. He was pressured 40% of the time at Jacksonville and finished at -5.6 EPA. At the Jets he was pressured 43.2%, sacked eight times and finished at -12.5. His per-dropback EPA of -0.014 (27th of 45) is an average of those two quarterbacks, not a picture of a middling one.

The sacks are a long-standing problem, not a one-season dip. His 12.1% sack rate ranks 44th of 45, and 39.6% of his pressures become sacks (34th of 37). Every Browns season has looked like this: 54.1% pressure-to-sack in 2022, 35.4% in 2023, 37.9% in 2024. Even in Houston he ranked near the bottom of the league in that stat. The line isn't helping. Cleveland's offensive hit rate is 31st, and the run game is 31st in EPA, so too many snaps become obvious passing downs. On third down he faces an average of 8.7 yards to go, converts 24.1% and has taken 8 sacks.

What keeps him afloat is the extended play. Twenty-two scrambles have averaged +0.455 EPA and moved the chains nine times. Once those are counted, his dropbacks add up to +2.9 EPA rather than the -2.8 his pure passing shows. When he does throw downfield it works: +0.473 EPA per attempt at 10+ air yards, almost all of it with Denzel Boston (+0.461 per target). The problem is underneath. Throws behind the line have cost -8.6 EPA, and his designed runs (-0.547 EPA, 35.3% stuffed) are a wasted call. He scrambles well and is a poor designed runner.

The direction is the worry. Over the last three games his per-dropback EPA fell to -0.095, his CPOE to -4.2 and his sack rate rose to 14%. The Browns went 2-1 in that stretch on the strength of a top-10 defense, not because of him. This is better than his 2024 (-0.229 EPA per play). It still looks like the Cleveland version of Watson, a passer whose good weeks depend on protection he usually doesn't get.

strengths.title: Scrambles turn broken plays positive
strengths.body: He leaves the pocket on 10% of dropbacks, and those plays have been his most reliable offense. Each scramble has averaged +0.455 EPA, and 9 of the 22 went for first downs. Running for 196 yards ranks him 3rd among quarterbacks. This is the payoff for holding the ball, and at 31 the legs still look like a sustainable part of his game.

strengths.title: Throws past ten yards pay
strengths.body: His 48 throws of 10+ air yards have produced +0.473 EPA per attempt and 22.7 total EPA. By contrast, throws under 10 air yards average only +0.041. Denzel Boston is the engine, with +0.461 EPA per target on 35 targets. The 19-attempt deep sample will cool, but the intermediate work with Boston has real volume behind it.

concerns.title: Sack rate is near league-worst
concerns.body: A 12.1% sack rate, 44th of 45, wipes out the value his scrambles and downfield throws create. Some of it is the line, which ranks 31st in hit rate allowed. But his pressure-to-sack rate has been bad every season of his career, and the 2.87-second time to throw shows he still waits for the play to develop. This won't fix itself; expect it to stay a problem.

concerns.title: Third downs are a dead zone
concerns.body: He converts 24.1% of third downs, with -0.238 EPA per play and a -10.3 CPOE. Some of that is situation: a 31st-ranked run game leaves him an average of 8.7 yards to go. Still, 8 sacks on 54 plays shows the long-yardage, obvious-pass downs are where the rush beats him most.

concerns.title: Short game and designed runs leak
concerns.body: Throws behind the line of scrimmage have cost -8.6 EPA, with a -9.4 CPOE on what should be easy completions. Designed runs have cost -9.3 EPA with zero explosive runs. These are the plays a play-caller uses to slow a pass rush, and right now they don't work, which leaves the offense with few counters to pressure.

trend.note: His best passing came in Weeks 2 and 4, behind clean pockets. Since then the Jets sacked him eight times, Baltimore held him to -6.9 EPA, and his last-three per-dropback EPA has dropped to -0.095 with a 14% sack rate.

nextGame.headline: Leaky Titans secondary, missing a starting safety, but they finish sacks
nextGame.body:
Tennessee is the weakest pass defense he has seen this year. It ranks 27th in pass EPA allowed and 26th on both deep and short throws, and it has given up big gains to secondary receivers. That suits a passer whose value comes on throws past ten yards. The catch is that the Titans' sack rate ranks 7th even though their hit rate ranks only 22nd. They convert pressure into sacks, which targets the one thing he does worst. Tennessee's offense is 31st in EPA, so the game should stay close and low-scoring (38.5 total, CLE -1.5). That keeps him in neutral states, where he has been roughly break-even, rather than in desperate catch-up mode.

Availability tilts toward Cleveland's passing game. Kevin Winston Jr., a safety who has played every snap, is out, and Tony Adams is questionable. That thins the back end exactly where Boston does his damage. On Cleveland's side, Quinshon Judkins is out and Dylan Sampson is still on injured reserve. That removes the lead back (60% of snaps) and a 19-target checkdown option from a run game that was already 31st. More of the offense lands on Watson, and more snaps become obvious passing downs.

keyMatchups.title: Boston versus a depleted secondary
keyMatchups.body: Boston is his most efficient target by a wide margin. Tennessee allows heavy EPA to second and third receivers and will play without Winston, its every-down safety. If Watson gets time, this is where the downfield value should come from.

keyMatchups.title: Titans finish sacks; he takes them
keyMatchups.body: Tennessee ranks 7th in sack rate on a middling hit rate, and Watson turns pressure into sacks as often as almost anyone. This one matchup decides whether the game looks like his Week 2 performance or his Week 5.

keyMatchups.title: Fannin into a stingy TE matchup
keyMatchups.body: Harold Fannin Jr. has been a solid middle-of-the-field option at +0.196 EPA per target. Tennessee has held top tight ends well under their averages, ranking 2nd by that measure. Expect the targets to tilt toward the wideouts.

nextGame.watch: His sack count. Three or fewer, and the weak Titans secondary should give him one of his better passing days; five or more, and it's another Jets game.

restOfSeason.body:
Expect roughly what he's been: around 190-215 passing yards a week, about one touchdown, and around 30 rushing yards mostly from scrambles. The legs and the Boston connection are the sustainable parts. The sack rate will probably drift down a little from 12.1%, but his career says it stays near the bottom of the league, which caps his efficiency. The +0.524 EPA on 19 deep throws and the 4 red-zone touchdowns on 16 attempts are small samples and likely to cool. The interception rate of 1.1%, about half the league average, is also probably better than his decision-making will keep producing. He has six fumble-type turnover-worthy plays already, and two have been lost.

The upside is Week 2- and Week 4-style games whenever the line holds up, and the schedule will decide some of that. The downside is that the run game shows no sign of helping, with Judkins hurt and Sampson still on the shelf. A pass-heavy offense with the 31st-ranked hit rate allowed leaves him exposed every week. A strong defense keeps Cleveland winning close games, but in the games he has played this year that has had little to do with him.
swingFactors: Pass protection and the sack rate
Judkins' return to steady the run game

confidence.note: Only six starts, but the sack problem matches his full career and his pressure-driven swings are consistent.
